discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can drive a time-reversal-invariant insulator into a new phase, the quantum spin Hall state. They introduced the Z2 topological invariant, which separates ordinary insulators from topological ones. In 2007 Molenkamp's group used carefully engineered HgTe quantum wells to measure quantized edge conductance, the first experimental proof of this phase. Together these results created a whole new class of quantum matter: two- and three-dimensional topological insulators, protected helical edge and surface states, and topological superconductivity. Hundreds of groups around the world now work in this area, including those studying moiré and van der Waals systems. The work shows how a deep theoretical idea and precise transport measurements on clean devices can together open an entirely new field of physics.
